matrix_resolution.proof: tests/test_living_agent_kernel_race_double_lease.py spawns two real subprocess daemons against one store, barrier-synchronized; asserts exactly one 'leased' transition + one wake_terminal_result per wake_id. ~940 races, 0 double-leases. Control experiment (separate lock paths, bypassing the service flock) reproduced a real DOUBLE-LEASE, proving the test can detect violations and that the flock is what closes the window.

lease_atomicity_caveat.finding: KernelRunStore.lease_next_wake is a lock-free read-modify-write; it is NOT atomic by itself. ALL concurrency safety lives in the service-layer fcntl.flock around run_kernel_daemon_service.
lease_atomicity_caveat.implication_1: Any caller invoking lease_next_wake / run_daemon_cycle DIRECTLY (not via the service, or with a non-shared lock path) WILL double-lease under contention.
lease_atomicity_caveat.implication_2: fcntl.flock is local-filesystem only. Coordinating daemons ACROSS HOSTS would NOT be serialized and could double-lease. The proven 'single OR coordinated' guarantee is single-machine. Cross-host coordination requires a distributed lock (not built).
lease_atomicity_caveat.scope_note: Consistent with the kernel's stated scope (single-machine agent operating contract). Flagged for the 'extremely autonomous, coordinated across many agents/machines' vision axis.

honest_state: All ten units are confirmed_green under independent adversarial verification. The LivingAgentKernel went from governed-skeleton (self-evolution existed only as field names) to a kernel that genuinely LEARNS (hash-chained per-agent lessons ledger + automatic run-level LEARN hook consuming proposed_learning_delta), EVOLVES under governance (skill_promote gated on operator-seeded evidence; self_edit confined to own-skill-files via the apply_patch denial ladder), HOLDS ITS OWN CONTEXT (durable wake/daemon-cycle ledgers that replay+verify from a fresh store), and RUNS single OR coordinated (a real subprocess daemon drains a mixed multi-agent queue end-to-end; no-double-lease proven under ~940 genuine OS-level races). One honest architectural caveat: lease atomicity is provided by the SERVICE flock, not the store primitive, and the flock is local-FS only — so cross-host coordination is the one unproven edge of the 'coordinated across many agents' claim. NOT YET DONE (explicit next axis, not part of this E2E build): wiring the kernel into a real production consumer (route an actual dharma_swarm persistent agent or hermes-m5 wake through it, default-off); live provider smoke under operator-approved budget (still fixture/injected); distributed lock for cross-host coordination.
